options.rationale: Correct: F = ma = 3 kg x 2 m/s2 = 6 N.

items.stem: Which TWO statements correctly describe Newton's third law? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Forces always occur in pairs that are equal in size and opposite in direction
options.rationale: Correct: this is the core of the third law.

options.text: The two forces in a pair act on different objects
options.rationale: Correct: action and reaction act on different bodies.

options.text: The two forces act on the same object and cancel out
options.rationale: Third-law pairs act on different objects, so they do not cancel.

options.text: The reaction force is always smaller than the action force
options.rationale: The paired forces are equal in size.

items.explanation: Correct: this is the core of the third law.

items.stem: Why does a passenger lurch forward when a car brakes suddenly?

options.text: Inertia keeps the passenger moving forward until a force stops them
options.rationale: Correct: by Newton's first law the body continues in motion until acted on by a force.

options.text: The car pushes the passenger forward
options.rationale: The car decelerates; the passenger continues due to inertia.
Gravity is unchanged; inertia explains the motion.
The seatbelt provides the backward force that stops them.

items.explanation: Correct: by Newton's first law the body continues in motion until acted on by a force.
